stories.summary: Apple on Tuesday unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac powered by its latest M6 chip, touting faster performance for running AI tasks directly on the devices. The MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 and the iMac at $1,499, with pre-orders opening Wednesday in 35 countries and availability from November 6. Apple says the MacBook Pro delivers up to 25% faster AI performance than its M5 predecessor, while the new iMac delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance than the previous M4 model.
stories.title: Apple launches M6 MacBook Pro and iMac with faster on-device AI

stories.summary: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce, as it looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments. Eligible staff include those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, while marketing, commercial business and security are excluded. The company has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for calendar 2026, mostly for AI data centers and chips.
stories.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 staff as AI spending soars

stories.summary: Several tech reviewers and industry analysts reported that their accounts on X were suddenly locked after they posted benchmark tests or comments about Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, with the platform accusing them of publishing undisclosed paid partnerships. Those caught up included neutral researchers who took part in blind tests on LMSYS Chatbot Arena and writers sharing public data from Artificial Analysis, as well as critics complaining about subscription throttling. To unlock their accounts, some bloggers were forced to add advertising labels and delete their posts.
stories.title: X locks accounts of AI reviewers posting about Kimi K3.1

stories.summary: Former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer defended using her AI prototype Dazzle to describe her daughter after a New York Times piece on the tool drew heavy criticism online. Mayer posted on X that she turned to the AI because she found the birthday assignment limiting, and shared more context behind the anecdote, while critics on X called the move bleak. The exchange has become a viral flashpoint over parents outsourcing personal writing to AI.
stories.title: Ex-Yahoo CEO defends using AI to describe her daughter amid backlash

stories.summary: Opera announced that its Opera One browser is the first of its browsers to offer built-in access to local AI models through the proposed WebAI standard, with Opera GX and Opera Neon to follow. At launch, users can tap into models from Google and Apple, including Google's Gemma and, on Macs, Apple's on-device foundation model, directly in Opera. The feature is opt-in with no subscription, and users control which websites can access local AI models.
stories.title: Opera One lets Mac users run Apple's AI model directly in browser

stories.summary: Mozilla announced two new features rolling out to Smart Window beta users in Firefox: AI-powered form filling and website monitoring. The form-filling feature can draw context from other open tabs to suggest answers for web forms, going beyond traditional autofill by generating responses from information on currently open pages. Mozilla notes the feature relies on Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite model to analyze form fields and extract details from selected tabs.
stories.title: Firefox Smart Window adds AI form autofill and website monitoring
